description: Signature edition. overview: In the Signature teaching of parasitology, What Parasitology Studies is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Parasitism means living at a host's expense, from benign to lethal. Helminths means parasitic worms, roundworms, tapeworms, and flukes with elaborate migrations. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Foundations material that follows.
core_concepts: Parasitism: living at a host's expense, from benign to lethal.
Helminths: parasitic worms, roundworms, tapeworms, and flukes with elaborate migrations.
key_laws: R0 for parasites: each infection must produce more than one new infection to persist.
vocabulary: Definitive host: where the parasite reproduces sexually.
Vector: an arthropod transmitting parasites between hosts.
methods: Microscopic diagnosis: identifying eggs, cysts, and blood stages morphologically.
history: Parasitology began with 19th-century discoveries of parasite life cycles, Ross and Grassi proving mosquito transmission of malaria around 1900. Chemotherapy, vector control, and molecular biology followed, though malaria and helminths still burden billions.
